name: KDE Connect
hook: Turns your phone and computer into one — clipboard, files, notifications, SMS, and remote control over your own Wi-Fi.
bullets: Share the clipboard, files, and links between phone and computer
See phone notifications on your desktop and reply to SMS from your keyboard
Use your phone as a wireless trackpad, media remote, or presentation clicker
Pause media, check battery, and find your phone — all encrypted and on your LAN
benefits: Continuity and Phone Link without locking you into Apple, Google, or Microsoft
Your data stays on your own Wi-Fi — no cloud relay account required
Answer texts and dismiss notifications without reaching for your phone
Turn an old phone into a keyboard, trackpad, and remote for your PC
setupSteps: Install KDE Connect on your computer (distro package, Windows or macOS build) and the app on your phone
Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi network
Open the app, tap the device shown in the list, and confirm the pairing code
Optionally grant notification, SMS, and storage permissions on Android
details: KDE Connect bridges your phone and your computer so they work as one. Pair them over the local network and you get a shared clipboard, file and link transfer, phone notifications mirrored to your desktop, the ability to reply to SMS from your keyboard, media playback control, a phone-as-trackpad remote, a presentation clicker, battery status, and a 'find my phone' ring. Everything is encrypted and runs directly over your own Wi-Fi with no cloud account and no Google or Microsoft services involved. It's developed by KDE, works on Linux (any desktop), Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS, and is licensed under GPL-2.0+.
setup: Install on both devices, then pair them
